subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Cold Brew vs. Iced Coffee
description: A fast breakdown of Cold Brew vs. Iced Coffee for builders.

hook.text: Cold brew and iced coffee taste completely different—even when made from the same beans.

buildup.text: Iced coffee is hot-brewed coffee poured over ice. It retains bright acidity from hot extraction.

discovery.text: Cold brew steeps grounds in cold water for 12–24 hours. Low temperature extracts fewer acids and less bitterness.

twist.text: Cold brew is a concentrate—typically 2x strength—meant to be diluted with water or milk.

climax.text: Japanese flash brew splits the difference: hot water drips onto ice, preserving aroma while chilling instantly.

punchline.text: Same beans, different physics, different drink entirely.

quiz.question: Why is cold brew less acidic than iced coffee?
options: Low temperature extracts fewer acid compounds
